title: Venial from imperfect work: could be mortal in kind, softened by how it is done
source_text: VIII. Venialia ex imperfectione operis ea dicunt, quae tametsi ex genere suo, mortalia esse possent, tamen ob imperfectionem operis venialia efficiuntur: quia videlicet, sola imperfectio operis facit, ut cum charitate & amore Dei pugnare non judicentur.
pass_a_gloss: They call venial from the imperfection of the work those which, although from their own kind they could be mortal, yet on account of the imperfection of the work are made venial: because, namely, the sole imperfection of the work makes them not to be judged as fighting with the charity and love of God.
pass_b_english: Some acts would be mortal by kind, yet imperfect performance keeps them from being judged as war on charity—hence venial.
Imperfect performance alone can keep an otherwise mortal kind from being judged as war on God’s love.

choices.why: Mode of acting that softens species.
